The criminal appeal under Section 378 of 'The Code of Criminal Procedure, 1973' (Hereinafter referred to as 'the Cr.P.C.') is directed against the judgment dated 26.09.2019 in CC No. 2668/2017 titled as 'Registrar of Companies vs. M/s. Gayatri Remedies Ltd. & Ors.' under Section 99 and 137 (3) of 'The Companies Act, 2013' (Hereinafter referred to as 'the Act') whereby the respondent No. 2 to 4 have been acquitted.

sentences.text: 3. Ld. Counsel for the appellant submitted that the appellant is entitled to prefer an appeal against a judgment of acquittal in view of amended section 372 of the Cr.P.C.
He submitted that after the Amendment Act 5 of 2009, a right of appeal to the victims has been incorporated and definition of 'victim' has been introduced in the Cr.P.C.

He submitted that appellant being the victim is entitled to prefer an appeal against the order of acquittal in a case under section 99 and 137 (3) of the Act.
4. Ld.

Counsel for the respondent No. 2 to submitted that right of appeal provided to the victim in amended section 372 of the Cr.P.C. is not meant for the complainant of a case under section 99 and 137 (3) of the Act.
submitted that appropriate remedy to the appellant is to seek special leave to appeal from the Hon'ble High Court of Delhi under section 378 (4) of the Cr.P.C.
He relied on judgment of the Hon'ble Supreme Court of India in Subhash Chand vs. State, (2013) 2 SCC 17.
He submitted that the present appeal is not maintainable.
6. The issue before this Court is no more res integra.

In 'The Bhajanpura Cooperative Urban Thrift &
Credit Society Ltd. vs. Prabhu Dayal' Crl. A. 972/2012 decided on 03.09.2014, the Hon'ble Delhi High Court considered remedy available in the case of acquittal in a case instituted on a complaint case, held as under"
"18.

entities.text:
Bhajanpura Cooperative Urban Thrift &
Credit Society Ltd. vs. Prabhu Dayal' Crl. A. 972/2012
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text:
Considering all the relevant provisions, I am of the considered view that the remedy available to the complainants under Section 138 N.I. Act against order of acquittal is only to seek special leave before filing an appeal under Section 378 (4)
Cr.P.C. before the High Court."

7. In Subhash Chand's (supra) case, the respondent instituted a complaint case against the appellant alleging therein that he violated certain provisions of the Prevention of Food Adulteration Act, 1994.
The appellant was acquitted by Ld. MM.
The State preferred criminal appeal in the Court of Session under Section 378 (1) (a) of the Cr.P.C.
The objection qua the maintainability of the said appeal in view of Section 378 (4) of the Cr.P.C. was rejected by the Court of Session.
8. In the said case, the appellant preferred a petition before the Hon'ble High Court of Delhi.
Hon'ble High Court of Delhi held that Court of Session has no jurisdiction to entertain an appeal filed in a complaint case.
The matter reached to the Hon'ble Supreme Court of India.

Hon'ble Supreme Court of India examined the issue whether in a complaint case, an appeal from an order of acquittal of the Magistrate would lie to the Sessions Court under Section 378 (1) (a) of the Cr.P.C. or to the High Court under Section 378 (4) of the Cr.P.C. Hon'ble Supreme Court of India

held that a complainant can file an application for special leave to appeal against an order of acquittal of any kind only to the High Court and the complainant cannot file such appeal in the Sessions Court, as under:

2 "21.

sentences.text: In view of the above, we conclude that a complainant can file an application for special leave to appeal against an order of acquittal of any kind only to the High Court.
He cannot file such appeal in the Sessions Court.

In the instant case the complaint alleging offences punishable under Section 16 (1) (1A) read with Section 7 of the PFA Act and the Rules is filed by complainant Shri Jaiswal, Local Health Authority through Delhi Administration.
The appellant was acquitted by the Metropolitan Magistrate, Patiala House Courts, New Delhi.

entities.text: Metropolitan Magistrate, Patiala House Courts, New Delhi
entities.label: COURT

sentences.text: The complainant can challenge the order of acquittal by filing an application for special leave to appeal in the Delhi High Court and not in the Sessions Court.
Therefore, the impugned order holding that this case is not governed by Section 378 (4) of the Code is quashed and set aside.

In the circumstances the appeal is allowed."
9.
Accordingly, the appellant cannot challenge the judgement of acquittal in a complaint case before the Sessions Court under section 378 (1) (a) of the Cr.P.C.
The remedy is to file an appeal to the High Court with special leave under section 378 (4) of the Cr.P.C.
The appeal filed by the appellant against the impugned judgment is dismissed.
A copy of this order be sent to Ld. trial Court for information.
Appeal file be consigned to record room.
